Build a suite of FREE web tools for the Nxeon marketing site at /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15, Tailwind v4, TypeScript). These are SEO magnets + genuinely useful utilities — they must cost nothing to run (no paid third-party APIs; use Node built-ins / client-side).

FIRST read the design system: components/marketing/primitives.tsx (PageHero, Section, SectionTitle, Eyebrow), components/marketing/sections.tsx (FeatureCard, CtaBand), components/marketing/icons.tsx, app/(marketing)/vps/page.tsx (structure), app/globals.css, lib/rate-limit.ts (checkRateLimit), app/api/track/route.ts (clientIp + API-route pattern), and how sitemap is generated (app/sitemap.ts).

BUILD a **/tools hub** + individual tool pages under app/(marketing)/tools/. Create a shared `ToolShell` component (components/marketing/ToolShell.tsx) that gives each tool a consistent layout: PageHero-style header (tool name + one-line description), the interactive tool UI card, and a short SEO content block ("What is X?", "How to use", "FAQ") below for search ranking. Each tool page has strong `export const metadata` (keyword-targeted title + description).

**Network tools** (server-side via API routes under app/api/tools/, each: validate input, **BLOCK SSRF** — reject private/loopback/link-local ranges 127.0.0.0/8, 10/8, 172.16-31, 192.168/16, 169.254/16, ::1, fc00::/7 and localhost — timeouts ≤5s, rate-limit per IP, cap output size):
- **WHOIS lookup** (/tools/whois) — query WHOIS for a domain (raw TCP socket to whois servers via node:net with IANA referral, OR `npm install whois` if simpler — verify it installs). Show registrar, dates, nameservers.
- **DNS lookup** (/tools/dns-lookup) — resolve A/AAAA/MX/TXT/NS/CNAME/SOA via node:dns/promises.
- **Port checker** (/tools/port-checker) — TCP connect to host:port (node:net), report open/closed + latency. Restrict to common/safe ports or any 1-65535 but SSRF-guard the host.
- **SSL certificate checker** (/tools/ssl-checker) — node:tls connect to host:443, show issuer, subject, validity dates, days-until-expiry, chain.
- **HTTP headers** (/tools/http-headers) — fetch a URL (SSRF-guarded, no redirects to internal), show status + response headers.
- **What's my IP** (/tools/my-ip) — show the visitor's IP (from x-forwarded-for) + reverse DNS.

**Client-side dev tools** (no server — instant, in the browser):
- **Password generator** (/tools/password-generator) — length + character-class options, crypto.getRandomValues.
- **Subnet / CIDR calculator** (/tools/subnet-calculator) — network/broadcast/host range/count from CIDR.
- **Base64 encode/decode** (/tools/base64), **JSON formatter/validator** (/tools/json-formatter), **UUID generator** (/tools/uuid-generator), **Hash generator** (/tools/hash-generator — SHA-1/256/512 via crypto.subtle).

The **/tools hub page** (app/(marketing)/tools/page.tsx): a grid of all tools (card per tool, icon + name + description, linking to each), with SEO metadata ("Free networking & developer tools — Nxeon").

INTEGRATE:
- Add **Tools** to nav: in components/marketing/MarketingHeader.tsx add a "Free tools" item to the `USE_CASES` array (or a top-level — keep it simple, use USE_CASES), and to components/marketing/MarketingFooter.tsx "Resources" column: `{ label: "Free tools", href: "/tools" }`.
- Add the tool routes to app/sitemap.ts so they're indexed.

RULES: use existing design tokens; keep every tool on-brand (dark navy/violet). "use server" files export only async functions. Client tool components are "use client". Do NOT edit prisma/schema.prisma, worker/*, app/layout.tsx. You MAY `npm install whois` (small, free) if you use it — verify clean install. Do NOT run build/tsc/prisma/commit. SSRF + rate-limit guards on ALL network tools are mandatory. Report every tool page created, the API routes, npm deps (if any), and the nav/sitemap edits.

Everything is wired up. Here is the complete report.

## Summary

Built a full suite of 12 free web tools for the Nxeon marketing site under `/tools`, on-brand with the existing design system (PageHero, Section, cards, brand tokens). All tools cost nothing to run — network tools use Node built-ins, client tools use browser crypto. **No new npm dependencies** (WHOIS is implemented with raw `node:net` sockets rather than the `whois` package).

Per instructions I did **not** run build/tsc/prisma or commit, and did not touch `prisma/schema.prisma`, `worker/*`, or `app/layout.tsx`.

### Shared infrastructure (new)
- `components/marketing/ToolShell.tsx` — consistent tool layout: header + tool card + SEO block ("What is X?" / "How to use" / FAQ) + related-tools sidebar; exports `FaqJsonLd` (emits `FAQPage` schema).
- `components/marketing/tools/ui.tsx` — client UI atoms (CopyButton, Field, ErrorNote, ResultCard, KeyValue, CodeOutput, RunButton).
- `lib/tools/net-guard.ts` — **SSRF guard**: resolves the host and rejects `127/8, 10/8, 172.16–31/12, 192.168/16, 169.254/16`, CGNAT, `0/8`, multicast/reserved, `::1`, `fc00::/7`, `fe80::/10`, IPv4-mapped v6, and `localhost`; connects to the vetted IP (defeats DNS rebinding). Exports `resolvePublicHost`, `isBlockedIp`, `extractHost`, `BlockedHostError`.
- `lib/tools/api.ts` — `clientIp` (x-forwarded-for), `toolRateLimit` (per-IP via existing `checkRateLimit`), `jsonError`, `readField`.
- `lib/tools/catalog.ts` — data-only tool registry (`TOOLS`, `TOOL_SLUGS`, `relatedTools`) shared by hub, sitemap, and pages.

### Tool pages (13 total) — each with keyword-targeted `metadata` + canonical
Hub: `app/(marketing)/tools/page.tsx` (title "Free Networking & Developer Tools — Nxeon", `ItemList` JSON-LD, category grid). Plus: `whois`, `dns-lookup`, `port-checker`, `ssl-checker`, `http-headers`, `my-ip`, `password-generator`, `subnet-calculator`, `base64`, `json-formatter`, `uuid-generator`, `hash-generator`.

### API routes (network tools, all SSRF-guarded + rate-limited + ≤5s timeout + capped output)
- `app/api/tools/whois/route.ts` — raw TCP port-43 WHOIS with IANA referral, parsed summary + raw.
- `app/api/tools/dns/route.ts` — A/AAAA/MX/TXT/NS/CNAME/SOA via `node:dns` Resolver.
- `app/api/tools/port-checker/route.ts` — TCP connect + latency (extra per-target sweep throttle).
- `app/api/tools/ssl-checker/route.ts` — `node:tls` cert issuer/subject/validity/days-to-expiry/SAN/chain.
- `app/api/tools/http-headers/route.ts` — status + headers, redirects reported not followed, no body read.
- `app/api/tools/my-ip/route.ts` — GET; IP + reverse DNS + version (also a JSON endpoint for `curl`).

Client-only tools (12 components in `components/marketing/tools/`) use `crypto.getRandomValues` / `crypto.randomUUID` / `crypto.subtle` — nothing leaves the browser.

### Integrations
- **Header** (`MarketingHeader.tsx`): added `{ label: "Free tools", href: "/tools", … , badge: "Free" }` to `USE_CASES`.
- **Footer** (`MarketingFooter.tsx`): added `{ label: "Free tools", href: "/tools" }` to the Resources column.
- **Sitemap** (`app/sitemap.ts`): added `/tools` plus all 12 tool routes via `TOOL_SLUGS`.
- **Docs** (`docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`): added a "Free tools suite" change-history section per project memory.

One note/tradeoff worth flagging: `http-headers` validates the host as public before `fetch`, but native `fetch` connects by hostname (can't easily pin the IP while preserving SNI/Host), so there's a theoretical sub-millisecond DNS-rebinding window there; the private-range rejection required by the spec is enforced. The other socket-based tools (port/ssl) connect to the pre-vetted IP directly.
